title: Lock the shared resource, not only the artifact
summary: A lock scoped to artifact or request identity prevents duplicate submissions of the same artifact but does not stop two different artifacts from concurrently mutating and superseding one shared resource.
ai_value: Helps deployment, publication, import, and migration agents choose lock granularity that protects the mutable target for the full mutation-plus-verification window.

contexts: operations mutate one shared downstream resource such as a deploy target, publication channel, import destination, migration target, or named environment
duplicate suppression is keyed by commit, image tag, filename, batch id, or request id
two different artifacts can be submitted concurrently

trigger_signals.description: Duplicate submissions of the same artifact are prevented, but two different artifacts still run concurrently.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: The lock key protects artifact identity, not the shared resource.

trigger_signals.description: Both operations log success while final state reflects only one artifact.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Success is local to each mutation; final shared-resource state may have superseded one result.

trigger_signals.description: A follow-up attempt risks rolling back newer work by redeploying or republishing its own artifact.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Re-read current target and require forward-only reconciliation before retry.

trigger_signals.description: The test suite uses two copies of the same artifact but not two different artifacts for the same resource.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Same-artifact tests prove duplicate suppression only; add a two-artifact resource contention test.

negative_signals.why_it_matters: Artifact-scoped suppression can be sufficient when there is no shared mutable target.

negative_signals.description: The downstream system enforces a forward-only compare-and-set or equivalent optimistic concurrency check on the shared resource.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Resource-wide locking is one safety design; a strong CAS can be the alternative with better throughput.

negative_signals.description: Head-of-line blocking would be worse than the risk and optimistic forward-only reconciliation is already enforced and tested.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Resource-wide locks trade throughput for safety; choose deliberately.

common_wrong_assumptions: A lock keyed by commit, tag, filename, or batch id protects the deployment or import target.
If both operations log success, both outcomes are still reflected.
Testing duplicate submission of the same artifact proves concurrency safety for different artifacts.

first_checks.check: Identify the mutable resource that must be single-writer for the whole mutation plus verification window.
first_checks.why: The lock key should match the hazard, not merely the request identity.

first_checks.check: Run a concurrency test with two different artifacts targeting the same resource.
first_checks.why: This is the discriminator that same-artifact duplicate tests miss.

first_checks.check: Assert the second operation waits or refuses before downstream mutation, and that release wakes only the next eligible waiter.
first_checks.why: Ordering must be enforced before the shared target changes.

first_checks.check: Re-read current target before retry and require forward-only reconciliation from the state observed at acquisition.
first_checks.why: Retries must not roll back newer work.

decision_rules.condition: Two different artifacts can mutate the same target concurrently under an artifact-scoped lock.
decision_rules.then: Lock the shared resource for the full mutation and verification window, while keeping artifact-scoped duplicate suppression as a lower layer.

decision_rules.condition: The downstream target enforces forward-only compare-and-set on current state.
decision_rules.then: A resource-wide lock may be unnecessary; keep the CAS evidence and test two-artifact races.

decision_rules.condition: A contender waits for the shared resource lock.
decision_rules.then: Record holder, arrival, target metadata, and wake only the next eligible waiter after release.

do_not: Do not claim concurrency safety from same-artifact duplicate tests alone.
Do not retry your artifact against a shared target without re-reading current state.
Do not choose resource-wide locking silently when throughput or head-of-line blocking is a real product tradeoff; consider forward-only CAS as an alternative.

Do not include private service names, internal URLs, account identifiers, incident identifiers, private repository paths, tenant/store names, setup-card field names, low-level endpoint strings or organization-specific tooling in public lessons.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Protect the mutable resource, test with two different artifacts, and require forward-only reconciliation before retrying after contention.

risk.notes: This public record is de-identified and does not authorize live mutation, publication, credential, permission, billing, data, or availability changes by itself.
